arxiv-1507-06000.title: On-line Survival Analysis of Power Electronic Converters Using Step Noise-Cox Processes
arxiv-1507-06000.creator: Pourya Shamsi 2
arxiv-1507-06000.description: Abstract This paper is focused on survival analysis of electrical components. The main goal of this paper is to develop a method for on-line estimation of the Mean Time To Failure (MTTF) of electrical components under dynamic stress levels. The proposed method models the variations of the stress levels as a stochastic process.

arxiv-2205-09979.title: Kilohertz Gravitational Waves from Binary Neutron Star Mergers: Inference of Postmerger Signals with the Einstein Telescope
arxiv-2205-09979.creator: Matteo Breschi, Rossella Gamba, Ssohrab Borhanian, Gregorio Carullo, Sebastiano Bernuzzi
arxiv-2205-09979.description: Abstract Next-generation detectors are expected to be sensitive to postmerger signals from binary neutron star coalescences and thus to directly probe the remnant dynamics. We investigate the scientific potential of postmerger detections with the Einstein Telescope using full Bayesian analyses with the state of the art waveform model NRPMw .

arxiv-2206-10310.title: Modeling Big Data based Systems through Ontological Trading
arxiv-2206-10310.creator: Luis Iribarne \corrauth, José Andrés Asensio, Nicolás Padilla, Javier Criado
arxiv-2206-10310.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Luis Iribarne \corrauth, José Andrés Asensio, Nicolás Padilla, Javier Criado. One of the great challenges the information society faces is dealing with the huge amount of information generated and handled daily on the Internet. Today, progress in Big Data proposals attempt to solve this problem, but there are certain limitations to information search and retrieval due basically to the large volumes handled, the heterogeneity of the information and its dispersion among a multitude of sources.

arxiv-2208-05358.title: CLEVR-Math: A Dataset for Compositional Language, Visual and Mathematical Reasoning
arxiv-2208-05358.creator: Adam Dahlgren Lindström, Savitha Sam Abraham
arxiv-2208-05358.description: Abstract We introduce CLEVR-Math, a multi-modal math word problems dataset consisting of simple math word problems involving addition/subtraction, represented partly by a textual description and partly by an image illustrating the scenario. The text describes actions performed on the scene that is depicted in the image.

arxiv-2310-04508.title: Boltzmann Equation Field Theory I: Ensemble Averages
arxiv-2310-04508.creator: Jun Yan Lau
arxiv-2310-04508.description: Abstract A quasi-nonlinear field theory which describes how to take ensemble averages that are unique to the Collisionless Boltzmann Equation is described. The assumption that the ensemble average of the distribution function is equal to the extremum entropy state, ⟨ f ⟩ = f 0 \langle f\rangle=f_{0} is taken apart and shown to be wrong.

arxiv-2405-05371.title: Coupling of the Finite Element Method with Physics Informed Neural Networks for the Multi-Fluid Flow Problem
arxiv-2405-05371.creator: Michel Nohra, Steven Dufour
arxiv-2405-05371.description: Abstract Multi-fluid flows are found in various industrial processes, including metal injection molding and 3D printing. The accuracy of multi-fluid flow modeling is determined by how well interfaces and capillary forces are represented. In this paper, the multi-fluid flow problem is discretized using a combination of a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) with a finite element discretization.

arxiv-2406-17847.title: Size matters: are we witnessing super-Eddington accretion in high-redshift black holes from JWST?
arxiv-2406-17847.creator: Alessandro Lupi ,, Alessandro Trinca, Marta Volonteri, Massimo Dotti, Chiara Mazzucchelli
arxiv-2406-17847.description: Abstract Observations by the James Webb Space Telescope of the Universe at z ≳ 4 z\gtrsim 4 have shown that massive black holes (MBHs) appear extremely overmassive compared to the local correlation for active galactic nuclei. In some cases, these objects might even reach half the stellar mass inferred for the galaxy.

arxiv-2503-02603.title: OkraLong: A Flexible Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Long-Text Query Processing
arxiv-2503-02603.creator: Yulong Hui, Yihao Liu, Yao Lu, Huanchen Zhang
arxiv-2503-02603.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) encounter challenges in efficiently processing long-text queries, as seen in applications like enterprise document analysis and financial report comprehension. While conventional solutions employ long-context processing or Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), they suffer from prohibitive input expenses or incomplete information.

arxiv-2504-03900.creator: Amelia Henkel, Francois Foucart, Selah Melfor, Samaya Nissanke, Alexandra Wernersson, Uddipta Bhardwaj

arxiv-2504-07085.title: Identifying Stochastic Dynamics via Finite expression methods
arxiv-2504-07085.creator: Senwei Liang Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory, Berkeley, CA 94720 SenweiLiang@lbl.gov Chunmei Wang Department of Mathematics, University of Florida, 1400 Stadium Rd, Gainesville, FL 32611, USA chunmei.wang@ufl.edu Xingjian Xu Department of Mathematics, University of Florida, 1400 Stadium Rd, Ga
arxiv-2504-07085.description: Abstract Modeling stochastic differential equations (SDEs) is crucial for understanding complex dynamical systems in various scientific fields. Recent methods often employ neural network-based models, which typically represent SDEs through a combination of deterministic and stochastic terms. However, these models usually lack interpretability and have difficulty in generalizing beyond their training domain.

arxiv-2507-00021.title: An Application of Fractional Calculus to Column Theory
arxiv-2507-00021.creator: José Villa-Morales, Manuel Ramírez-Aranda
arxiv-2507-00021.description: Abstract In this article, we employ a fractional version of the radius of curvature in Euler’s equation for column buckling, enabling us to derive a fractional differential equation in the Caputo sense. We solve this equation and demonstrate that for certain values of the fractional parameter, there exists a critical buckling force.

arxiv-2512-09312.title: Tyche: A Hybrid Computation Framework of Illumination Pattern for Satellite Beam Hopping
arxiv-2512-09312.creator: Ziheng Yang, Kun Qiu, Zhe Chen, Wenjun Zhu, Yue Gao
arxiv-2512-09312.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ziheng Yang, Kun Qiu, Zhe Chen, Wenjun Zhu, Yue Gao. High-Throughput Satellites (HTS) use beam hopping to handle non-uniform and time-varying ground traffic demand. A significant technical challenge in beam hopping is the computation of effective illumination patterns. Traditional algorithms, like the genetic algorithm, require over 300 seconds to compute a single illumination pattern for just 37 cells, whereas modern HTS typically covers over 300 cells, rendering current methods impractical for real-world applications.
